top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) remains my choice on the common criteria. Public knowledge of Blinding, the first volume of the Orbitor trilogy, and of Solenoid indicates a distinctive voice, formal ambition in the architecture of very large books, and imaginative and intellectual depth: memory, the body, dream and cosmology are built into one cumulative project. The citation in the slate is a single writer, a prose oeuvre with the poetry named only as its root, and that scope is one the committee can defend. The agreement of all six round-2 files is not evidence of merit and I have not counted it. My preference is provisional. I judge the Romanian prose through translation and secondary description, I have not read the texts, and whether the later long works enlarge the project or restate its motifs is unresolved. Adonis would be the first alternative if expert reports pointed that way, but he is not on this slate. Nothing in the evidence supports no award (P000) over a laureate, so it is ranked last.
recusal_note: none apparent from the profile; disclosed without adjudication: elected to the Academy alongside Steve Sem-Sandberg in 2020, married to a former finance minister, Permanent Secretary since 1 June 2026. None of these is connected to the shortlisted writer on the supplied record. Her committee voting status as a co-opted member is undocumented, and the simulated vote is a modeling assumption.
